cause: While driving across a flat concrete plaza and curving right toward a row of parked scooters and trash bins, the robot failed to detect a stationary small rover parked in front of a recycling bin and collided with it at t=8.25 s at ~0.7 m/s. The provided IMU log disagrees strongly with the video (showing extreme vertical acceleration spikes such as az_g = -1.901 g while the robot sits motionless on flat pavement), so the video is trusted over the corrupted or mismatched IMU log.
evidence: 00:00.000-00:01.500: Robot is stationary on flat dry concrete, whereas the IMU log reports severe vertical anomalies (az_g = -0.014 g at t=0.72 s, 0.065 g at t=0.92 s, and -1.901 g at t=1.58 s), proving the IMU log is corrupted or mismatched.
00:01.625-00:03.000: Robot rotates left in place, pauses until 00:03.625, then drives forward.
00:05.750-00:06.000: A stationary small 4-wheel robot (~0.4 m size, radius ~0.2 m) becomes visible ~1.8 m ahead, parked directly in front of a brown recycling bin.
00:06.000-00:08.250: Robot steers rightward at ~0.7-0.8 m/s directly toward the parked robot without stopping.
00:08.250-00:08.375: Front-right of the ego robot collides with the stationary robot, pushing it slightly before coming to a halt.
00:09.500-00:11.875: Robot reverses away from the obstacle and turns left.

other_factors: Cluttered environment with parked scooters, bicycles, and recycling bins
Obstacle is another low-profile small wheeled robot parked against a bin
IMU log disagrees with video (spurious -1.9 g vertical spikes while stationary on flat ground); video is trusted

unknowns: Exact impact acceleration and robot speed from sensors because the IMU log is corrupted or mismatched with the video clip
